doc.title: Bobby Johnson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: The Survivors with Milt Hinton, Clark Terry and others
summary: He recalls a group organised by Arnie Lawrence with Hinton, Panama Francis, Clark Terry, and his friend George Kelly.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: I understand that you got to play with Milt Hinton in a group called The Survivors?

Well I was with Cab Calloway with Milt Hinton. As a matter of fact I have a tape, would you like it? Yeah, I have a tape that was taken at one of the music schools. I won’t give them a plug. But Arnie Lawrence, you’ve heard of him.

He got together a bunch of older guys, like Panama Francis on drums, myself, Milt Hinton on bass, the great Clark Terry — can you think of Clark Terry as an old man? Clark Terry on trumpet, Red Richards, God rest his soul he just passed away, Red Richards. Then Eddie Barefield, and we recorded. I’ll give you one of the tapes, and Milt Hinton is — I was with Milt Hinton when he was young with Cab Calloway — when the whole world was young — with Cab Calloway. You have heard of Panama Francis?
He’s sick now. Then George Kelly, a great tenor player. I just saw him in “Moscow on the Hudson.” Did you see the movie?
He and I came up together as kids, in the south, you know what I mean? And I just saw him. And we never did think that we’d get this old, but God kept us here, you know?
